reason: The text (Exodus 14) describes Yahweh saving and protecting the Hebrews from Egyptian pursuit. Yahweh fights for the Hebrews and destroys the Egyptians, not the Hebrews. The passage shows the Hebrews responding to Yahweh's deliverance with fear and belief (וַיִּֽירְאוּ הָעָ֖ם אֶת־ יְהוָ֑ה וַיַּֽאֲמִ֙ינוּ֙ בַּֽיהוָה - they feared Yahweh and believed in Him). There is no conditional threat that Yahweh will kill the Hebrews if they don't worship properly, nor any reference to improper worship or its consequences.
